title: NBA Suspends Clippers Owner Ballmer After Leonard Salary Probe
summary: The NBA stripped the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round draft picks and suspended owner Steve Ballmer for one year after finding the team had circumvented salary cap rules by facilitating sponsorship agreements between outside companies and star player Kawhi Leonard. Randall Williams reports on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Japanese Companies Consider Asset Sales as Yen Debt Costs Rise
summary: Japanese companies are expanding their toolkit to deal with the steepest borrowing costs in a generation, including considering sales of strategic shareholdings and other assets to offset the impact, a Bloomberg News survey shows.

title: Aurora Cannabis Board Recommends Rejecting Curaleaf Bid
summary: Aurora Cannabis CEO Miguel Martin called a takeover bid from cannabis company Curaleaf 'inadequate' and said that it was not in shareholder's best interest after the company's board unanimously rejected the offer. Martin said that he is not against offers on principle and would recommend going with another bid if it had the right value and structure for shareholders. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Elliott Builds Deutsche Telekom Stake, Opposes T-Mobile Merger
summary: Elliott Investment Management has built a sizeable stake in Deutsche Telekom AG and indicated the German telecommunications giant should ditch a potential merger with its American arm T-Mobile US Inc., people familiar with the matter said.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 2
summary: Oil steadied near the highest closing level in five weeks as fighting again raged between the US and Iran, renewing the threat to energy exports from the Middle East.

title: Anthropic’s Mega-IPO Plan Looms Over IPO Market
summary: Anthropic's IPO is casting a long shadow over companies’ US listing plans, as they try to find room for their deals to grab attention after the Sept. 7 Labor Day holiday. Scarlet Fu reports on Bloomberg Deals. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Will Not Tackle Debt Until Republicans, Democrats Come Together, Says Rep. Arrington
summary: House Budget Chairman Jodey Arrington said 'Republicans and Democrats are going to have to come together' on a debt reduction plan to counteract the demographic challenges of increasing Social Security and Medicare beneficiaries. Arrington also discussed the pushback against AI data centers around the country, saying that the US has win the AI race but there should be guardrails on drawing on energy and water resources to do so.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Broadcom Needs Nvidia-Like Earnings to Stop $520 Billion Skid
summary: Broadcom Inc. has had a difficult summer in the stock market, as a disappointing outlook sent the shares on a roughly $520 billion tailspin since hitting a high in early June.

title: MLB's Angels Sold For Record $4B
summary: Bloomberg's Randall Williams joins Dani Burger and Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Billionaire Stan Kroenke is expanding his sports empire with the addition of the Los Angeles Angels. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment bought a controlling stake with a valuation at $4B. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: KKR Scores Windfall in $17B Sale of USI Insurance
summary: Bloomberg's Allison McNeely joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." KKR is set to reap a $3.3 billion windfall from its deal to sell USI Insurance Services to Aonfor $17 billion, a significant exit for a unit that’s invested its balance sheet in long-term private equity bets. (Source: Bloomberg)
